sentences.text: Due to a matrimonial dispute between the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.4, a First Information Report dated 6.4.2022 giving rise to Case Crime No.0016 of 2022 under sections 498-A, 323, 506 and 307 IPC and sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Firozabad was lodged by respondent no.4.
The matter was referred to Mediation Centre.
However, it did not succeed as the parties could not come to terms.
The police after investigation submitted a charge sheet against petitioner nos.2 and 3.

The petitioner nos.2 and 3 namely Rakesh Kumar Agrawal and Smt. Sarita Agrawal respectively filed an application under Ankit Agrawal And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69192490/
1 section 482 Cr.P.C. being Application No.47818 of 2023.

entities.text: Ankit Agrawal And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the meantime, the parties had entered into a compromise and they had agreed to separate.
The compromise was also verified by the Court where the divorce petition was filed.
In this view of the matter, the Application U/S 482 No.47818 of 2023 was allowed by this Court on 18.1.2024.

The same is being reproduced here as under :-
"1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Amrik Shanker Dubey, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants for quashing the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 7919 of 2023 (State Vs. Rakesh Kumar Agrawal and Another) under Sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Firozabad pending in the court of Civil Judge (JD)/FTC-II, Firozabad including charge sheet dated 04.11.2022 arising out of Case Crime No. 0016 of 2022 on the basis of the compromise dated 06.05.2023 entered between the parties.

entities.text: Criminal Case No. 7919 of 2023 (State Vs. Rakesh Kumar Agrawal and Another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Thana, District Firozabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that in pursuance of the order dated 15.09.2023 passed in Application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No.34203 of 2023 parties have appeared before the court below for verification.

He submits that the compromise has already been entered between the parties on 6.5.2023 and the same has been verified by the court concerned on 11.10.2023, therefore, the present case be finally decided.
4. Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has not disputed the facts as stated by learned counsel for the applicants.
He further contended that opposite party no.2 does not want to proceed with the criminal case against the applicants and the same may be quashed.
5. Learned AGA does not dispute the fact that parties have entered into settlement which is duly verified by the court concerned.
It is further submitted that he would have no objection in case criminal proceedings are put to an end.
He further submits that in view of settlement there is virtually no chance of any conviction being recorded in the criminal proceedings.

6. Having examined the matter in its totality, this Court is of the view that the criminal proceedings in the present case had essentially been an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and there are no such over bearing circumstances for which the applicants ought to be prosecuted even after the parties has entered into a settlement.

Needless to observe that with the present stand of the parties in terms of their settlement, there is practically no chance of recording conviction, even if the case under the F.I.R. in question is put to trial.
In other words, entire exercise of trial would only be an exercise in futility.

On the contrary, looking to the nature of dispute and the fact that the disputants being the close relatives, have compromised and want to proceed peacefully ahead, it would be in the interest of justice that criminal Ankit Agrawal And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69192490/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: proceedings in question are quashed.

7. It would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that the criminal case is put to an end.

8. In view of the fact that the parties do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them and the fact that matter has been mutually settled between the parties in view of the compromise dated 6.5.2023, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Parbatbhai Aahir Vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303 and State of M.P. Vs. Laxmi Narayan, (2019) 5 SCC 688, the proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners states that in view of the terms which had been entered into and also verified by the court, the FIR dated 6.4.2022 giving rise to Case Crime No.0016 of 2022 under sections 498-A, 323, 506 and 307 IPC and sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Firozabad be also quashed.
3.
Sri Amrit Shankar Dubey, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.4 does not dispute that compromise had been entered into.
He also agrees that the FIR impugned in the instant petition be quashed.
4. Under such circumstances, we are of the view that no useful purpose would be served by further investigating into the case in pursuance of the FIR dated 6.4.2022.

The FIR dated 6.4.2022 giving rise to Case Crime No.0016 of 2022 under sections 498-A, 323, 506 and 307 IPC and sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Firozabad is, accordingly,
quashed.

Also, if any investigation is taken place and any police report has been submitted vis.-a-vis.
petitioner nos.1, 4 and 5, that would also stand quashed.
5. The writ petition is, accordingly, allowed to the extent indicated above.

Order Date :- 29.5.2025 GS (Madan Pal Singh, J.) (Siddhartha Varma, J.)
